name: Nate
reason: The Chinese surname 'Nie' (Tower Master Nie of the Rune Tower) was localized to the phonetically similar US name 'Nate'.
description: A senior rune authority in the Heartlands, renowned as one of its foremost runic experts whose opinions shaped Guild policy for three decades (Eps 502-505). He and his colleagues, who had begged for access to the Tower for years, are left humiliated and awestruck when Zane renders their life's work obsolete.

name: Demon Emperor Corpse
reason: The source term 'Yin Corpse Demon Emperor' (also 'Demon Emperor Yin Corpse') was compressed to 'Demon Emperor Corpse' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A towering, mindless undead automaton encountered in Ep 534, standing three times a person's height and programmed only to kill. Tia dispatches it before leading her group onward, mirroring Ning Yudie's defeat of the Yin Corpse Demon Emperor in the source (ch 521).

name: Serpentine Sword
reason: The source's descriptive term 'snake-shaped sword' (the Divine Kingdom Prince's curved Low Saint rank blade) was localized as the more evocative 'Serpentine Sword'.
description: A curved, snake-shaped sword wielded by a Divine Kingdom prince against Zane (Eps 547-548). When swung it manifests a Demonic Dragon, a dragon-headed serpent of energy that coils around its wielder and lunges at foes.

name: Kingsley
reason: The source character 'Lord Jing' of the Purple Heart Holy Land was localized to 'Kingsley', a dignified US name echoing the 'Jing' sound and his lordly station.
description: A senior figure associated with the Sanctuary (source: Purple Heart Holy Lands) in the Tower of Sin arc (Eps 579-620). He explains the Tower's seat system to Zane, noting that a seat grants the right to enter the top of the Tower, and later deliberates with the Sanctuary elders over Zane's feats.

name: Don
issues: Most extracted mentions are 'Don't' sentence fragments from unrelated episodes; the real character Don appears only in Eps 580-581.
reason: An unnamed Ogre (Demon Race) War Lord from the source's Tower of Sin arc was given the short, blunt US name 'Don' in the adaptation.
description: The first Ogre War Lord Zane faces inside the Tower of Sin (Eps 580-581). He intends only to frighten a human War Fighter, but Zane's fearless aura crushes him, leaving him trembling and fuming yet unwilling to step forward.

name: Madeline
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Xia Shuang' was fully localized to 'Madeline', an elegant US name suiting her status as a revered seat holder.
description: The Demon Night's seat holder in the Tower of Sin (Eps 598-608), reputedly only a tenth-level War Lord but with a soul already at the Fighting Soul Realm; onlookers say anyone who eyes her with impure thoughts gets burned. She studies the wall of names where Zane, a mere human War Fighter, has claimed a first-row spot, mirroring Xia Shuang seeing Luo Zheng's name placed beside hers in the source.

name: House Drew
reason: The source's 'Zhuo Family' of Cloud Sea City was localized to 'House Drew', keeping the 'Zhuo'/'Drew' sound while fitting the adaptation's Legacy House naming scheme.
description: A Third-Grade House in Cloudhaven (Ep 525, source: the Zhuo Family, a third-grade aristocratic family of Cloud Sea City). Its members are outraged when Elder Imogen passes a coveted title to Tia instead of one of their own (Ep 711), and its younger generation watches sourly as its champions are beaten down (Ep 715).

name: Faye
issues: Likely two different characters share the name: Owen's girlfriend with a Violet-Core Physique, sealed by Maddox in the Ethereal Spirit Sect (Eps 760-765), and Cora's maid (Eps 933-934). They should not be merged.
reason: 'Faye' is an adaptation-assigned US name; no named source counterpart appears in the evidence.
description: In Eps 760-765, Faye is Owen's girlfriend, one of the women with a Violet-Core Physique whom Maddox imprisoned and held in sensory-sealed stasis alongside Elara until Zane's party frees her. A separate 'Faye' appears in Eps 933-934 as Cora's maid, sent to fetch mulled cider.

name: Ethereal Spirit Hall
reason: The source term 'Void Spirit Palace' (seat of the Void Spirit Sect) was localized as 'Ethereal Spirit Hall' to match the show's 'Ethereal Spirit Sect' naming.
description: The main hall of the Ethereal Spirit Sect (Eps 762-765), the site Maddox had seized as his headquarters. Zane is returned there after his trial, and he and his loved ones take a quiet forest walk before reluctantly heading back to it.

name: Renzo
reason: 'Renzo' is a localized name for one of Zane's male traveling companions in this arc (the source trio Zuo Chuandong / Lan Chen / Yue Ying); the evidence does not settle which of the two men he corresponds to.
description: One of Zane's companions in Eps 797-846 who, with Camilla and Barry, spars with Zane at his request so he can study their techniques. He later owes Zane his life and stands stunned as the reality of his rescue settles over him.

name: Saroyan
reason: An unnamed Devil Clan Battle-Saint from the source (chs 919-920) was given the name 'Saroyan' in the adaptation.
description: An Ogre War Sage of the fourth level whom Zane confronts in Ep 942, eerily pinpointing the exact remaining length of his life. After Zane snaps his mid-grade Relic saber bare-handed, Saroyan, of a race that does not flee, flees anyway and is killed in a single exchange.

name: Ailsa
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Liu Lan' was fully localized to 'Ailsa', a distinctive feminine name for the possessed Demon Night War Sage.
description: A third-level War Sage of the Demon Night (Eps 948-954) whose body is possessed by the Queen of Punishment; when she speaks, every member of the Demon Night drops to one knee. Because the Queen is working through Ailsa's limited vessel, her strength is only a fraction of what it should be, paralleling Liu Lan, the third-rank Battle-Saint who turns on Liu Yu in the source.

name: Bridget
reason: 'Bridget' is an adaptation-assigned US name for a disciple in the sect-recruitment scenes; no named source counterpart appears in the evidence.
description: A disciple accompanying her master, the beautiful sect mistress who comes to recruit Cora (Eps 966-967). Her prepared opening speech dies in her throat, and she rises to take her master's arm as the woman glides over to Cora.

name: Krista
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Hua Bingyan' was fully localized to 'Krista', a sharp feminine name fitting the cold, possessive sect recruiter.
description: A sect mistress determined to claim Cora, whose First-Rank Violet-Core Physique she has no intention of letting go (Eps 967-968). When Cora flatly refuses to join her sect or become her student, Krista laughs coldly and argues with the rival recruiter Leah until Elder Apeiron turns a cold glance on her, paralleling Hua Bingyan's rebuked claim over Xi Youqin in the source.

name: Siren’s Kiss Sect
reason: The source's 'Soul Stirring Tower', whose women cultivate an Art of Seduction that drains men dry, was renamed 'Siren's Kiss Sect' to convey the same allure-and-death idea in a Western register.
description: A sect of seductresses few men dare enter (Eps 967-968): the promise of pleasure is a powerful lure, but joining tends to cost the men their vitality or their lives, matching the source's Soul Stirring Tower whose seduction arts squeeze cultivators dry.

name: Codex of Ascension
reason: The unnamed, worn thread-bound book Luo Zheng studies by lamplight in the source's opening chapters was given the proper title 'Codex of Ascension' for the adaptation.
description: The book Zane desperately studies by lamplight in the Lowell House cellar (Eps 1-3), vowing to complete it within a month. It corresponds to the worn manual of the source's opening, the burning of which reveals the hidden gold leaf that changes Luo Zheng's fate.

name: Paige
issues: Name reused for two apparently different characters: a member of Felix Sterling's entourage (Eps 99-101) and a fighter grouped with Cassian, Maren and Taryn in the late Queen of Punishment arc (Eps 1161-1178); they should not be merged.
reason: 'Paige' is an adaptation-assigned US name; no named source counterpart appears in the evidence.
description: In Eps 99-101, Paige is one of Felix's entourage, a woman whose straight hair writhes and twists itself into five sharp spiraling points when she attacks. The name later reappears (Eps 1161-1178) for a fighter paired with Cassian, Maren and Taryn, apparently a different character.

name: Sunstone Citadel
reason: The source's imperial power 'Burning Sky Palace' was plausibly localized as 'Sunstone Citadel', keeping the solar/fire imagery while fitting the Western fantasy register.
description: A great protective power of the Empire (Eps 87-142) whose combined shield with the Skyreach Sect has kept demons out for years, leaving most apprentices ignorant of how dangerous demons truly are.

name: Johnson
reason: 'Johnson' is an adaptation-assigned US name for a minor sect pledge; no named source counterpart appears in the evidence.
description: A pledge at the sect (Eps 106-107) who forces himself forward with every pledge watching, then retreats in stunned silence, his reputation crumbling with each backward step.

name: Sentinel Peaks
reason: The source's '33 peaks of Qingyun Peak' (the Blue Cloud Sect's ranked peaks) was localized as the 'Sentinel Peaks' of the Skyreach Sect.
description: The ranked peaks that make up the Skyreach Sect (Eps 75-115); Sunflower Ridge is the fourth-ranked among them. Becoming the top pledge of any Sentinel Peak is said to be impossible through hard work alone, echoing the source's line about the sect's 33 peaks.

name: Bone Spikes
reason: A descriptive demonic attack from the source's demon-general fights was rendered as the capitalized technique 'Bone Spikes'.
description: Razor-sharp spikes of bone shot from the body as a weapon (Eps 113-140): first a demon general's nasty trick against Zane, and later an ability Zane himself unleashes, erupting dozens of spikes from his back into an Armored Wyvern.

name: Twin Blades
reason: The paired 'butterfly blade' from the source's armory scene (ch 128) was localized as the 'Twin Blades' to read naturally as a matched weapon set.
description: Dalton's signature paired weapons (Eps 117, 142), honed alongside his Forbidden Techniques through countless hours of painful practice; per the master localization sheet they are classed as Legendary Arms in Ep 142. They are introduced in the same armory scene as the spear Tronson, mirroring the source's butterfly blade hanging beside the broken spear Piercing Mountain.

name: Howard
issues: Two different characters share the name: a Stormcrown Peak apprentice ranked near Felix and Preston Sterling (Ep 118), and Elder Howard (= source Elder Wei) who brings Zane to the Baptism by Laws with a drop of True Dragon's blood (Eps 438-449). They should not be merged.
reason: The source's 'Elder Wei' was localized as 'Elder Howard', a solid, senior-sounding US name for the elder who sponsors Zane's climb.
description: Elder Howard (Eps 438-449) is the old man who brought Zane to the Rising Dragon Platform, securing the city lord's special approval and spending a drop of True Dragon's blood on him. Having written the boy off, he watches in slack-jawed disbelief as Zane grasps the Spatial Law's first level in under six hours and later breaks through to the Fighting Soul level. A separate minor 'Howard' is a Stormcrown Peak apprentice in Ep 118.

name: Corefire
reason: The source term 'Earth Core Fire' was compressed to 'Corefire' for a punchier Western fantasy register.
description: A ferocious elemental fire found in a forbidden lake that Zane dives into (Ep 69) and later absorbs repeatedly (through Ep 212). Absorbing it once caused a Spirit Rune to appear on his chest, marking him as a Psionic Weapon, matching the source's terrifying Earth Core Fire bursting from pools of magma.

name: Dreadlord
reason: The source's demon leadership rank 'Demon King' was renamed 'Dreadlord' to avoid royal-title confusion and fit the Western fantasy register.
description: An elite demon rank whose demonic energy dwarfs anything a human could sustain (Eps 136-140). Four Dreadlords, including Aldrich and Orion, lead the assault on Silverspire; if the city's champion lost her duel, the Dreadlords would finish the city.

name: Tronson
reason: The source spear 'Piercing Mountain', a broken long spear with a crystal set in its tip, was renamed 'Tronson' in the adaptation.
description: A broken spear with a crystal embedded at its tip (Eps 142-187), prized for its barrier-penetrating power though insufficient against Yolande's particularly sophisticated wards. Zane extracts its Emerald Crystal at the Elysian Keep and embeds it in his left arm, where it later erupts with brilliant crimson energy.

name: House Sutton
reason: The source's 'Yu Family' of the Forbidden City was localized as 'House Sutton' under the adaptation's Legacy House naming scheme.
description: A powerful house (Eps 147-302) whose two guards Zane drops in a heartbeat, their weapons clattering uselessly beside them, mirroring the source's two slain Yu Family guards. The house later extends its protection over a fugitive, at least for a time.

name: House Pauling
reason: 'House Pauling' is an adaptation-created Great House name; no clear source counterpart appears in the evidence.
description: One of the Great Houses (Eps 148-188), counting Walsh and Leon among its people per the master localization sheet. The house is cold-blooded about its own: to House Pauling, Walsh was an acceptable loss.

name: Sandra
reason: 'Sandra' is an adaptation-assigned US name for a minor character in the Immortal Mansion arc; no named source counterpart appears in the evidence.
description: A woman in the cipher episode of the hidden-mansion arc (Eps 154-155) who refuses to trust Zane, stepping back from the cipher with trembling fingers; her distrust helps set the Soul Realm masters slaughtering one another.

name: Desperate Melee
reason: The source term 'Life Ending Battle' was renamed 'Desperate Melee' to fit the Western fantasy register.
description: A deadly trap-battle that Zane accidentally triggered on his first visit to the mansion (Ep 154) and that is deliberately reprised much later (Eps 1186-1189) as Saul's improvised, unrepeatable gambit; the source's Life Ending Battle shows the same early and late chapter spread.

name: Province of Galeria
reason: The source's 'Mok Province' was plausibly localized as the 'Province of Galeria' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A province of the Empire visited in Eps 167-195, aligning with the source's Mok Province arc (chs ~180-194) involving the Mo Family.

name: Lightning Horse
reason: The source mount 'Chasing Lightning Colt', a precious fast steed of the Eastern Domain, was simplified to 'Lightning Horse'.
description: A prized steed Zane acquires for travel (Eps 167-168). Its pace starts out average, but as it builds momentum it accelerates into a blur of motion, true to the spiritual-beast horse it adapts from the source.

name: Sky-Shatter Cudgel
reason: The source weapon 'Tian Jue Cudgel' (also rendered 'Tian Jue Stick') was localized as 'Sky-Shatter Cudgel', translating the sense of the Chinese name into English.
description: Heavy cudgels designed to hit with unmatched, pulverizing force, wielded by a squad of four men against Zane (Eps 168-169). Their blows are shaken off by Zane's body, mirroring the source's Tian Jue Stick rebounding off Luo Zheng.

name: Vivian
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhuo Fei' was fully localized to 'Vivian', a sharp feminine name for the dart-wielding attacker.
description: A fierce fighter who attacks Zane alongside Frey (Eps 170-173), flicking volleys of willow leaf darts with blinding speed and vowing to kill him, directly matching the source's Zhuo Fei, who harried Luo Zheng with willow leaf darts.

name: Novak Family
reason: The family name derives from the adaptation's mentor character Isla Novak; no distinct source counterpart for the family appears in the evidence.
description: The family of Zane's mentor Isla Novak, mentioned once in Ep 171.
